Stop JupyterLite deleting files dropped onto their folder's breadcrumb

## References

Fixes #20423

## Code changes

- In `BreadCrumbs._evtDrop`, skips invoking `renameFile` when the target breadcrumb path is the same as the file's current location (`newPath === localPath`), matching the existing non-moving file check in `DirListing`.
- Adds unit tests in `BreadCrumbs` testing that dropping a file onto its current directory or server root breadcrumb is ignored without triggering renames.

> **Added by a maintainer**
>
> - Refuses a breadcrumb as a drop target when none of the dragged items would move.

## User-facing changes

> **Added by a maintainer**
>
> Dropping a file onto the root or preferred breadcrumb while the file browser shows that folder renamed the file onto itself:
>
> - In JupyterLite the file was deleted (seen on 0.8.7 and 0.9.0b1). A folder disappeared from the file browser and a "Move Error" dialog opened (https://github.com/jupyterlite/jupyterlite/issues/2111)
> - With Jupyter Server, when the file was open in an editor, its next save overwrote changes that another program had made to the file. The "File Changed" dialog did not open.
>
> The breadcrumbs now refuse such a drop.
>
> A second file browser can come from an extension. When that browser shows `docs` and the default file browser shows `docs/img`, a file dragged from `docs` onto the `img` breadcrumb now moves into `docs/img`. JupyterLab 4.6.6 refuses that drop.

## Backwards-incompatible changes

None

Stop UI mode's test explorer flashing a parent row red after a passing run (PILOT-1178) ## What this changes In UI mode, the test explorer no longer flashes rows red. A row used to play a 0.6 s red flash (`te-status-flash-failed`, keyframes `flash-fail`) whenever its status went from `running` to `failed`. File, describe and project rows take their status from all their children. So when you ran a passing test next to one that had already failed, those parent rows went from `running` back to `failed` and flashed, as if the test you just ran had failed (PILOT-1178). The flash is removed entirely. Playwright's UI mode has no such flash, and the status icon already shows the result. - `TestExplorer.tsx`: the `TreeNode` effect and state that set the flash class are gone, along with the hook imports that only they used. - `ui-mode.css.ts`: the `.te-node.te-status-flash-failed` rule and `@keyframes flash-fail` are deleted. - `trace-viewer.css.ts`: the hand-synced copy of `@keyframes flash-fail` is deleted too. Nothing used it. Statuses themselves are unchanged. After the run, the parent rows still show the failed icon, because the earlier failure still decides their status. ## How it was tested - **New hermetic web test** in `web-tests/ui-mode/specs/test-explorer.spec.ts` ("no row flashes when a passing test runs beside an earlier failure"): - It fails test A, then replays the message sequence the UI server sends for a single-test run of test B: `run-start`, `file-status running`, `test-start`, `test-status passed`, `file-status done`, `run-end`. - It records every CSS `animationstart` and asserts that none fired on a `treeitem` row. As a check that the recorder works, it also asserts that the running spinner's `spin` animation was recorded. - Written first. Before the fix it failed with two `flash-fail` animations, on the file row and the describe row. - Package checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `knip` in `packages/tapsmith`; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `web-tests`. - 390 web tests passed. - One unrelated test, `live-locators.spec.ts` › "a pick on an Android mirror maps the pointer in pixels…", fails on this machine. It fails the same way with this branch's source changes reverted to `origin/main`, and it passes in `main`'s CI. - `/review-loop`: clean after 1 round (no findings). - Device QA (`/qa-this-branch`) was skipped as trivial. The change only deletes a cosmetic animation in the web app. A device adds nothing beyond the hermetic suite, which drives the same app with the UI server's real message sequence. ## Decisions made in auto mode - **Remove the flash, or keep it on test rows only?** I removed it entirely, as the ticket suggests. The alternative was to flash only `test` leaf rows. That would keep a cue on the row that actually failed, but it adds little beyond the change of icon, and Playwright's UI mode has nothing like it. - **Skip device QA?** Yes, because the change is trivial (see above). The alternative was a full `/qa-this-branch` cycle on a leased device. ## Checklist - [x] My contributions are signed off (`git commit -s`, or individual remediation) -- see [the contribution guide](https://github.com/tapsmith/tapsmith/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#sign-off-your-commits) - [x] Existing tests pass - [x] New behaviour is tested at the lowest tier that can actually cover it - [na] `docs/api-reference.md` is updated, if this changes public API (no public API change) - [na] Proto changes are handled in both the TypeScript SDK and the Rust daemon, if applicable 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01FJuVgQa2Z6KyNeRKoZkBjM --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? stores: TransactionsStore: reset payment state behind graph sync prompt

# Description

On embedded LND mainnet with express graph sync off (the default) and "Never ask again" not chosen, `TransactionsStore.sendPayment` parks the request in `pendingPaymentData`, opens the graph sync prompt and returns early without resetting `loading`, `status`, `payment_hash` or `payment_preimage`. `PaymentRequest` and the keysend path in `Send` navigate to `SendingLightning` regardless, so from the second payment of a session the screen behind the prompt shows the previous payment's outcome, including "Payment successfully sent" with the previous hash and preimage. `hideGraphSyncPrompt()`, which the modal's `onClosed` calls on swipe, backdrop tap and back button, only hid the prompt, so that stale outcome stayed as the result of a payment that was never handed to LND. With tips enabled, the stale success also sent the tip.

This PR:
- clears the outcome fields and sets `loading` when the prompt holds a payment back, so the screen shows the spinner behind the prompt. The reset is a new `resetPaymentOutcome()` that `sendPaymentInternal` also calls, so both paths clear the same fields, including `paymentOutcomeUnverified` (without it, a previous payment's "ZEUS stopped checking this payment" warning showed next to "Payment was not sent")
- in `hideGraphSyncPrompt()`, drops a payment that is still held back and reports "Payment was not sent" (new `views.GraphSyncPrompt.paymentNotSent` string)
- in `proceedWithPayment()`, takes the request out of `pendingPaymentData` before hiding the prompt, so the modal's later `onClosed` does not report the dispatched payment as not sent

Neither path touches the state while another payment is in flight. "Ignore once" and "Never ask again" behave as before. "Enable & Restart" now also shows "Payment was not sent" until the restart, after which the saved payment is offered again as before.

Not in this PR: the callers still navigate to `SendingLightning` before the prompt is answered.
